## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect than by the stem galls it induces on oak tissue. In Florida, Disholcaspis quercusomnivora is associated with Chapman oak, especially in scrub, sandhill, pine-oak woodland, and other dry upland habitats where this white oak occurs. The larva develops protected inside the gall, which provides both food and shelter, while the gall itself can support a specialized community of parasitoids, inquilines, and other gall-associated insects.
